summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of gastroparesis, gastrostomy, and a gastric pacemaker was admitted for severe abdominal pain and vomiting. Imaging revealed cecal volvulus with ischemia, likely caused by entanglement of the bowel with the pacemaker wires. She underwent an exploratory laparotomy, right hemicolectomy, ileotransverse anastomosis, stomach repair, and removal of the gastric pacemaker and wires. Postoperatively, she had ongoing nausea and difficulty tolerating oral intake, but gradually improved with tube feeds and diet advancement. A gastric emptying study was normal, but an upper GI series showed moderate esophageal dysmotility. She tolerated a regular diet and full tube feeds by discharge, with stable vital signs and healing incisions. She was discharged home with home health services for GJ tube care and follow-up with gastroenterology for esophageal evaluation.
